newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Top British banker slams single Euro currency.
newsitem.headline: Top British banker slams single Euro currency.

text.p: The chief executive of one of Britain's biggest banks said on Thursday the British public did not want a single European currency, so it should not be forced on them.
"It's very clear that the vast majority of people in the UK don't want it," Peter Birch, chief executive of Abbey National plc , told Reuters in an interview at a banking conference.
"When people don't want something, why force it down their throats?"

The top banker was speaking as tension over the future of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) mounted a day after a row erupted between the German central bank and government over conditions for EMU.
He added that the efforts to secure monetary union were "politically driven" and said the French people had also shown they did not want a single currency in the recent election.
Birch questioned attempts to form a "United States of Europe" saying that Europe should not attempt to mirror the United States.
"I believe that if a common currency is forced through by the politicians in Europe, it could well end in tears in a few years' time."
He said a crisis could then be possible in some countries when in 10 years' time they might decide to abandon the euro.
Birch said it was possible that Britain could enter EMU in the first wave in 1999 even though the new Labour government has said it would only do so if it was in the British interest.

"We just have to be very careful before we do that. Trading in Europe is one thing but a common currency is very different. I think the current government is very sensitive to what people want and will tread very carefully before they ram it down our throats."
Birch said Britain should be in control of its own destiny, not Brussels.
"If we relinquish control of the currency, then somebody else is in control of our destiny."
